beats.lead: One jellyfish species can reverse its own ageing.
beats.text: Turritopsis dohrnii, the immortal jellyfish, can revert from a mature adult back into an immature polyp and start its life cycle over.
beats.note: It does this through transdifferentiation, where mature cells switch into entirely different cell types. Starvation, physical injury, or a sudden change in temperature or salinity can trigger it.

beats.name: Shin Kubota
beats.role: a biologist at Kyoto University, kept a colony of the jellyfish alive long enough to watch it rejuvenate itself 11 times over two years, the only person known to have managed it for any length of time.

beats.lead: The claim of immortality has a real catch.
beats.text: In the wild, almost every individual is eaten or falls ill long before it ever needs to rejuvenate.
beats.note: Researchers are careful to call this biological immortality rather than invulnerability. Predation and disease still kill most of them outright.

beats.text: The species has also quietly spread to every ocean on Earth, carried in the ballast water of cargo ships.
beats.note: A Smithsonian scientist called it a worldwide silent invasion. At about 4.5 millimetres across, it is easy to overlook.

beats.text: In 2022, researchers compared its genome to a jellyfish that ages normally and found real differences in how it repairs DNA and renews stem cells, clues that could one day inform human ageing research.

beats.line: The only animal known to hit rewind on its own life cycle.
